FDI is associated both with higher economic growth and with higher levels of inequality in the host country.
FDI and state capacity are complementary in the process of economic development.

FDI and domestic private investment are equally productive in the initial years of investment, but FDI has a larger effect over the long term; and the impact of FDI is conditional on the quality of the state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the state as a mediator of the impact of FDI on growth in transition economies.
the impact of foreign investment on economic development in transition economies.
the question of how the state shapes the impact of foreign investment on economic development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FDI is a positive contributor to economic development in transition economies, but that its effect is conditional on the quality of the institutional environment.
FDI is not the panacea for development that it is often claimed to be.
FDI is a good thing, provided that the host country has a relatively strong state.

the impact of foreign investment on growth is conditional on the quality of institutions in the host economy.
